title: Global Payments Report 2026: Merchants Can Make Payments Pay—Acquirers Can Help Them
gist: BCG's 2026 survey of ~500 large merchants finds payments costs keep rising despite professionalization, but the 12% who combine dedicated teams, smart orchestration, and a profit-center mindset outperform on conversion, authorization, and fraud metrics, while acquirers face a widening satisfaction gap and a looming competitive fight with big tech platforms over agentic commerce.

insights.claim: 79% of large merchants report payments costs rose over the past five years and fewer than 1 in 10 managed to bring costs down, showing that staffing up payments teams alone does not control spend.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Signals a structural, industry-wide payments cost problem that vendors selling cost-optimization or orchestration tools can target as a large addressable pain point.
insights.quote: 79% reported that their payments costs had risen over the previous five years, and less than one in ten said that they had managed to bring them down.
insights.locator: The payments process has become more costly

insights.claim: Among surveyed merchants, 89% have dedicated payments teams, 43% use dynamic orchestration or a deliberate single-acquirer model, and 28% treat payments as a profit center, but only 12% combine all three practices together.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: The gap between having payments infrastructure (89%) and having the full integrated model (12%) marks a large underserved market for consulting/software that helps merchants close it.
insights.locator: Most Merchants Have the Pieces, but Few Have the Model

insights.claim: 72% of large merchants still run payments purely to cut complexity and cost, while the 28% that treat payments as a profit center use closed-loop wallets, co-branded cards, embedded finance, and loyalty integration to generate revenue and deepen customer relationships.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Investors evaluating merchant/retail operating efficiency should treat 'payments as profit center' adoption as a proxy for more sophisticated, higher-margin operating discipline.
insights.locator: For 72% of large merchants, the payments mandate still centers on reducing complexity

insights.claim: Profit-center merchants track authorization rates 21 percentage points more often, fraud false-positive rates 17pp more, conversion 12pp more, and review acquirers annually 8pp more than cost-center merchants, indicating that revenue framing drives measurement rigor.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Measurement rigor (tracking authorization/false-positive/conversion rates) is a leading indicator of which merchants will extract more value from payments and be better acquirer customers to win.
insights.locator: They also manage payments more rigorously.

insights.claim: The 12% of merchants combining dedicated teams, smart orchestration, and profit-center framing show 2 percentage points higher conversion and authorization success, 0.5pp lower fraud rates, and 1pp lower legitimate-transaction blocking than the survey average.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Quantifies the ROI of full payments-model adoption, giving a benchmark for what 'best-in-class' payments performance is worth in basis points of conversion and fraud.
insights.locator: The 12% of large merchants that combine all three practices

insights.claim: Netflix uses layered fraud-recovery systems with machine-learning routing, decline-specific retry timing, and multichannel dunning to help keep monthly churn at 2-3%, among the lowest in streaming.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Illustrates a concrete mechanism (ML-based payment retry/dunning) that directly reduces subscription churn, a metric investors track closely for streaming/subscription businesses.
insights.locator: Netflix uses this approach as part of a payments model

insights.claim: More payment providers do not necessarily mean better performance: a leading French sports brand runs an in-house orchestration layer across multiple acquirers, while Louis Vuitton consolidated onto a single global acquirer to unify in-store and online infrastructure, and both approaches work when matched to the merchant's scale and capabilities.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Challenges the assumption that multi-acquirer orchestration is always superior; investors assessing payments vendors should note that single-acquirer consolidation deals remain a viable, competing strategy for large luxury/retail brands.
insights.locator: Match the acquiring model to the business.

insights.claim: Payment systems wrongly decline 2% to 5% of legitimate transactions, yet nearly half of merchants never quantify these false positives, meaning fraud-prevention performance is commonly overstated by ignoring lost good-customer revenue.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: A blind spot this large (2-5% of legitimate sales falsely declined, unmeasured by ~50% of merchants) represents a quantifiable revenue-recovery opportunity for adaptive ML fraud vendors.
insights.quote: Payment systems can wrongly decline 2% to 5% of legitimate transactions, yet nearly half of merchants never quantify these false positives.
insights.locator: Measure fraud and false positives together.

themes.theme: Measured ROI from fixing the payments model

insights.claim: A global fashion and sports retailer traced payments costs and performance across its five most important markets and achieved savings equal to 15% to 20% of its annual payments costs.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Provides a concrete savings benchmark (15-20% of payments spend) that investors can use to size the value-creation opportunity from a targeted payments cost audit.
insights.locator: A global fashion and sports retailer performed this analysis

insights.claim: A global cruise line centralized its payments strategy under one operating plan, cutting processing and vendor costs by $10 million and quadrupling royalty revenue from its co-branded card program.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: A 4x increase in co-branded card royalty revenue shows how much upside is left on the table when payments is centrally managed as a growth lever rather than a decentralized cost function.
insights.locator: A global cruise line used this approach to centralize its payments strategy

insights.claim: Among acquirers named as a primary provider by at least ten respondents, the share of very satisfied merchants ranges from 17% to 71%, a 54-point spread, with price the leading reason merchants consider switching, followed by declining authorization rates, reliability, and fraud prevention.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: A 54-point satisfaction spread plus 44% of merchants having switched/added a provider in five years signals real, measurable share-shift risk for weaker acquirers as merchants adopt dynamic orchestration to compare performance.
insights.quote: That 54-point spread leaves weaker incumbents exposed as merchants gain better tools to compare performance and move volume.

insights.claim: 39% of merchants use different acquirers for online and in-store transactions, and bringing in specialized product experts to solve complex use cases can lift merchants' adoption of value-added services by up to 12 percentage points.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Omnichannel consolidation and specialist advisory services are concrete cross-sell levers acquirers can use to grow wallet share and defend against the churn risk highlighted by the satisfaction spread.
insights.locator: Compete on value beyond the rate card.

themes.theme: Agentic commerce as the next battleground

insights.claim: 73% of merchants say they would switch acquirers for better support with agent-initiated transactions (agent authentication, tokenization, delegated consent, liability rules), making agentic-commerce readiness a near-term competitive differentiator for acquirers.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: A 73% willingness-to-switch figure signals that agentic-commerce infrastructure capability could soon become a primary acquirer selection criterion, ahead of legacy price/reliability factors.
insights.quote: 73% of merchants say that they would switch acquirers for better support in this area
insights.locator: Help merchants prepare for agent-led commerce.

insights.claim: 31% of merchants name acquirers or payment service providers as their preferred partner for agent-led commerce, second only to large technology platforms, suggesting acquirers can still capture transaction-level value even if big tech platforms own the customer interface.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/stanislas-nowicki
insights.so_what: Frames the competitive structure of agentic commerce as a layered market: big tech platforms will likely dominate the interface while acquirers compete for the transaction layer, which affects where payments-value accrues.
insights.quote: Although platforms may own the interface, acquirers can differentiate in the transaction itself and capture more of the resulting volume.
insights.locator: In BCG's survey, 73% of merchants say that they would switch
